claims.claim: A project charter formally authorizes a project and gives the project manager authority to apply organizational resources to project activities.
A charter can provide a high-level project record, including purpose, objectives, requirements, risks, approval information, assigned manager authority, and authorizing sponsor information.
A charter is an early high-level record rather than a complete detailed project plan.
A project manager’s authority originates in the authorization described by the charter and is not equivalent to unlimited organizational authority.
Major assumptions, constraints, and risks can be recorded separately so later decisions can distinguish provisional conditions, limits, and potential effects.
A charter should not be represented as a legal contract or a guarantee of project outcomes.
